gdp_2025.label: Real GDP growth
gdp_2025.quote: Economic growth in Tanzania accelerated to 5.9 percent in 2025

gdp_q1_2026.label: Real GDP growth, first quarter
gdp_q1_2026.note: Based on the rebased national accounts (base year 2019), which break the data series (Box 1, p. 5).

gdp_rebased.label: National accounts rebased
gdp_rebased.quote: updating the GDP base year from 2015 to 2019

gdp_medium.label: Projected real GDP growth, medium term

gdp_20y.label: Average annual growth
gdp_20y.quote: grown by an annual average of 5.7 percent over the last two decades

gov_share.label: Share of 2025 growth driven by government spending
gov_share.quote: over two-thirds of economic growth was on the back of government spending

services_half.label: Share of 2025 real growth from services
services_half.quote: Almost half of the real growth in 2025 came from services

sec_services.label: Services growth
sec_services.quote: the service sector, already the largest sector, expanded by 6.7 percent

unemployment.label: Unemployment (World Bank estimate)
unemployment.quote: unemployment in 2025 at 6.1 percent, down from 8.7 percent in 2020

poverty.label: Share living below the $4.20/day poverty line (estimate)
poverty.note: Down from 70% in 2018, the most recent official year.

food_insecure.label: People facing acute food insecurity
food_insecure.quote: about 1 million people (10 percent of the analyzed population) are currently facing acute food insecurity

infl_band.label: Bank of Tanzania medium-term inflation target band

infl_jul26.label: Headline inflation, year-on-year
infl_jul26.quote: Headline inflation rose to 4.2 percent year-on-year in July 2026

cbr.label: Central Bank Rate
cbr.quote: raised the CBR by 50 basis points to 6.25 percent

diesel.label: Rise in domestic diesel pump prices
diesel.period: Start of the war to June 2026
diesel.quote: Domestic diesel pump prices increased by about 60 percent

credit.label: Private sector credit growth, year-on-year
credit.quote: Private sector credit growth accelerated to 28.1 percent year-on-year in June 2026

rev_target.label: Domestic revenue against target
rev_target.quote: exceeded the target by about 4.2 percent in the first eleven months of FY26

tax_target.label: Tax revenue against target
tax_target.quote: consistently exceeded targets during the first eleven months of FY26 by 9.1 percent

spend_target.label: Total spending against estimate
spend_target.quote: total spending fell short of the estimate by 5 percent

debt_jun26.label: Public debt, % of GDP
debt_jun26.quote: stood at 49 percent of GDP at end-June 2026

debt_risk.label: Risk of debt distress
debt_risk.quote: The risk of debt distress remains moderate

cad_fy26.label: Current account deficit, % of GDP (US$2.3 billion)
cad_fy26.quote: widened to US$2.3 billion, or 2.5 percent of GDP, in the year ending June 2026

cad_2025.label: Current account deficit, % of GDP (US$2.0 billion)
cad_2025.quote: from US$2.0 billion, or 2.2 percent of GDP, in 2025

goods_exports.label: Goods exports growth (estimate)
goods_exports.quote: Goods exports are estimated to have increased by 19.2 percent in FY26

service_exports.label: Service exports growth, to US$8.1 billion
service_exports.quote: Service exports also increased by 14.4 percent to US$8.1 billion

imports.label: Imports of goods and services growth, to US$20.8 billion
imports.quote: Imports of goods and services increased by 18.1 percent to US$20.8 billion in FY2026

tourists.label: International tourist arrivals
tourists.quote: 4.5 percent rise in international tourist arrivals

emp_ratio.label: Employment-to-population ratio
emp_ratio.quote: employment-to-population ratio of 68.7% is among the highest in the world

labor_force.label: Labour force (12.8 million women, 14.5 million men)
labor_force.quote: labor force consists of 27.3 million people

median_pay.label: Median hourly pay, including profits and in-kind income (about US$0.40)
median_pay.quote: the median hourly pay, including profits and in-kind income, is just TZS 1,005

status_split.label: Own-account workers / contributing family workers / employees, % of workers
status_split.quote: own-account workers (75%) or contributing family workers (17%), with employees accounting for just 8 percent

agri_share.label: Share of workers employed in agriculture
agri_share.quote: it remains the dominant sector, employing 54% of workers

informality.label: Informality
informality.quote: informality has deepened from approximately 93% in 2020 to around 95% in 2024

working_age.label: People reaching and leaving working age each year
working_age.quote: approximately 2 million Tanzanians reach working age while only around 400,000 leave it

hq_jobs.label: High-quality jobs, out of 26 million total jobs
hq_jobs.quote: Out of Tanzania’s 26 million total jobs, we find evidence of only about 550,000 high-quality jobs

hq_private.label: High-quality jobs in the private sector
hq_private.quote: Only about 120,000 of these jobs are in the private sector

decent_pay.label: Hourly wage the report uses as "decent pay" (about US$1.50)

women_share.label: Women: share of working-age population / of workers / of high-quality jobs
women_share.quote: Women constitute 51% of the working-age population, and 46% of all represented workers. Yet, they represent only 32%

youth_share.label: Youth (15–35): share of working-age population / of workers / of high-quality jobs
youth_share.quote: constitute about 63% of the working age population, 46% of all workers, but only 34%

hq_tax.label: Holders of high-quality jobs vs regular jobs who pay income tax
hq_tax.quote: 96% of holders pay income taxes, compared to just 7% of regular job holders

high_ready.label: Workers with high readiness and opportunity
high_ready.quote: only about 15% of Tanzanian workers have high readiness

q1.label: Labour force with low readiness and low opportunity (Q1)
q1.quote: Most Tanzanians in the labor force — over half — face the dual constraints of low readiness and limited market opportunities

q2.label: Labour force with capability but no credentials or connections (Q2)
q2.quote: A further 15% of the labor force has demonstrated capability

q3.label: Labour force in high-opportunity places but not ready (Q3)
q3.quote: About 18% of the labor force operates in high-opportunity environments

q4.label: Labour force with high readiness and high opportunity (Q4)
q4.quote: The 15% of the labor force in Quadrant 4

secondary.label: Secondary school-aged children enrolled
secondary.quote: only around 40% of secondary school-aged children enrolled

care.label: Share of time on unpaid care work, women vs men
care.quote: Women spend about 14% of their time on unpaid care work, compared to about 4% for men

women_micro.label: How much less productive women-led microenterprises are
women_micro.quote: 46% less productive than those run by men

skills_gap.label: Advertised positions requiring skills applicants often lack
skills_gap.quote: Around 83% of advertised positions in Tanzania require skills that the current pool of applicants often lacks

sa_spend.label: Social assistance spending, % of GDP: Tanzania vs SSA and LMIC averages
sa_spend.quote: Social assistance spending across all programs amounts to 0.7% of GDP, compared to SSA and LMIC averages of 1.6%

pssn.label: Share of households below the poverty line PSSN III will cover
pssn.quote: will cover only 13% of households below the national poverty line

inspectors.label: Formal firms reached by labour inspectors each year
inspectors.quote: labor inspectors reach less than 5% of formal firms annually

prod_gap.label: Labour productivity vs SSA average: services / manufacturing
prod_gap.quote: approximately 49 percent lower in services and 70 percent lower in manufacturing than the SSA average

young_firms.label: Formal firms that are young (began after 2018): Tanzania vs Rwanda (Ghana 26%)
young_firms.quote: only 12% of formal firms were young firms

young_peers.label: Young formal firms: Rwanda / Ghana
young_peers.quote: far fewer than Rwanda’s 38% or Ghana’s 26%

young_prod.label: Young formal firms with above-median productivity (about twice that among peers)

unregistered.label: Firms that started operating without registration (25% in 2013)
unregistered.quote: 32% of firms reported starting operations without registration up from 25% in 2013

fdi.label: Foreign direct investment
fdi.quote: FDI in Tanzania has hovered around 2% of GDP since 2016

bready_entry.label: B-Ready score for business entry (top 20% globally)

foreign_reg.label: Cost of registering a foreign firm, % of gross national income per capita
foreign_reg.quote: 59% of gross national income per capita

mgmt_time.label: Senior management time spent on regulatory compliance (2% in 2013; regional average 8%)
mgmt_time.quote: almost 14% of senior management’s time on regulatory compliance

insolvency.label: B-Ready score for business insolvency (bottom 20% globally)

invest_11.label: What the average firm invests now, compared with a decade ago
invest_11.quote: the average firm now invests just 11% of what it did a decade ago

innov_tz.label: Tanzania: licensed foreign tech / R&D / website / process innovation / new product, %

credit_constrained.label: Firms fully or partially credit constrained: Tanzania vs SSA average
credit_constrained.quote: One out of three companies in Tanzania reports being fully or partially credit constrained (the average in SSA economies is 22%)

bank_finance.label: Firms financing investment through banks: Tanzania vs Côte d’Ivoire / Rwanda
bank_finance.quote: Only 14% of firms finance investments through banks, compared with 38% in Côte d’Ivoire and 25% in Rwanda

land.label: Large firms citing land access as a major constraint: Tanzania vs SSA average
land.quote: 58% of large firms in Tanzania reported access to land to be a major or very severe constraint to operation compared to an average of 20% in SSA economies

skilled.label: Skilled share of manufacturing workers (85% in 2013)
skilled.quote: While 78% of workers in Tanzania’s manufacturing sector can be described as skilled

training.label: Firms offering formal training
training.quote: With 20% of firms offering formal training to their workers

spread.label: Productivity of top 10% vs bottom 10% firms: Tanzania vs aspirational peers
spread.quote: about 32 times more productive than those in the bottom 10% - compared to a gap of about 17 times among aspirational peers

frontier.label: Share of jobs in frontier (top 10% most productive) firms
frontier.quote: In 2023 they accounted for only 18% of jobs

frontier_sales.label: Frontier firms’ share of sales
frontier_sales.quote: they accounted for 97% of sales in 2013

frontier_wages.label: Frontier firms’ average wages vs other firms
frontier_wages.quote: They also pay, on average, four times higher wages

exports_2026.label: Real export growth
exports_2026.quote: Real export growth is expected to rebound strongly to 6.8% in 2026

industry_2026.label: Industry growth
industry_2026.quote: Industry is projected to sustain strong growth of 7.8%

infl_2026.label: Inflation
infl_2026.quote: reflected in 4.1 percent inflation expected in 2026

deficit_2026.label: Fiscal deficit, % of GDP
deficit_2026.quote: The fiscal deficit will narrow to 3.1% of GDP

tax_gdp.label: Tax-to-GDP ratio the fiscal framework assumes
tax_gdp.quote: raising the tax-to-GDP ratio from 13% to 16% over the medium term

tourism_exports.label: Tourism receipts, share of exports
tourism_exports.quote: which account for around 24% of Tanzania’s exports

transport_exports.label: Transport service exports, share of exports
transport_exports.quote: transport service exports which account for 15% of exports

risks.label: Balance of risks
risks.quote: The balance of risks is tilted to the downside, with domestic reform capacity, fiscal discipline, and external shocks as the key concerns

human_capital.label: Most consequential medium-term policy choice
human_capital.quote: the most consequential policy choice is the sustained prioritization of human capital spending

climate_drought.label: People exposed and vulnerable to significant drought
climate_drought.quote: 5 million Tanzanians are exposed and vulnerable to a significant drought

climate_flood.label: People exposed and vulnerable to flooding
climate_flood.quote: 700,000 Tanzanians are exposed and vulnerable to flooding

climate_heat.label: People exposed and vulnerable to heatwaves
climate_heat.quote: 600,000 are exposed and vulnerable to heatwaves

climate_multi.label: People exposed and vulnerable to multiple risks at once
climate_multi.quote: A further 400,000 are exposed and vulnerable to multiple risks at the same time

edu_premium.label: Extra pay in formal private jobs for workers with lower secondary vs primary education
edu_premium.quote: Workers with lower secondary education earn 22%–30% more in formal private sector jobs than those with only primary education

tvet_gain.label: Earnings gain from TVET for workers with formal wage contracts
tvet_gain.quote: TVET generates earnings gains of up to 51% for workers with formal wage contracts

oda_halved.label: Official development assistance as a share of GDP since 2010
oda_halved.quote: ODA has halved as a share of GDP since 2010

oda_grants.label: Share of ODA provided as grants
oda_grants.quote: while about 65 percent of ODA was provided as grants in 2010, less than 40 percent is now grant-financed

labour_exports.label: Labour-intensive exports (manufactured and horticultural goods)
labour_exports.quote: This represents an underutilized opportunity for Tanzania

mobile_money.label: Tanzanians reached by mobile money
mobile_money.quote: Mobile money now reaches over 94% of Tanzanians

generational.label: When the institutions that decide the jobs trajectory get built
generational.quote: the institutions built in the next five years will determine whether that trajectory bends upward

evidence_thin.label: Impact evidence for labour programmes outside PSSN
evidence_thin.quote: the evidence base outside PSSN is thin

leave_to_learn.label: How most training programmes are designed (excludes Q1 and Q2 workers)
leave_to_learn.quote: most are designed on a leave-to-learn model

wb_pillars.label: The report’s policy framework
wb_pillars.quote: Two policy pillars address these interlocking constraints

jobs_quality.label: The report’s central finding
jobs_quality.quote: Tanzania does not face a jobs shortage, it faces a jobs quality challenge

high_pay.label: 1.5 times the median wage, a benchmark for high pay
high_pay.quote: 1.5 times the median wage (TZS 1,507 per hour, a benchmark for high pay)

establishments.label: Establishments in the 2023/24 Statistical Business Register (12.2% employ five or more)

five_plus.label: Firms employing five or more workers
five_plus.quote: with only 12.2% of firms employing five or more workers

early_marriage.label: Girls who marry before age 18 (UNICEF 2022, cited)
early_marriage.quote: About one-third of girls marry before age 18

nonconcessional.label: Non-concessional external borrowing, share of public debt
nonconcessional.quote: accounting for close to one-fifth of total public debt

limited_spending.label: Business environment fixes could yield gains with limited public spending
limited_spending.quote: could yield substantial gains with relatively limited public spending

climate_belt.label: Where exposed and least able to cope cluster
climate_belt.quote: cluster in a diagonal belt through the center of the country
